"NVDA IS FUCKED" - GUIDEPOINT GLOBAL, PROBABLY We believe investors are overly focused on NVDA's income statement, when the balance sheet looks like Ceuta's Border Patrol Our forensic balance sheet analysis uncovered the following discrepancies. Please note that we are all Chartered Financial Analysts and our findings are GIPS-Compliant. 1. Inventories went up $4B. Why would inventories go up, instead of being sold? Because demand was ZERO. This $4B will hit the income statement at $0 revenue and 0% GM next quarter. 2. PP&E went up by $2 billion. We believe they are hiding a Guangzhou coal mining company inside PP&E, which would dilute NVDA's multiple. Investors think NVDA is an AI play, when it's really a coal miner that isn't even GIPS-compliant. So now you have gross margin pressure paired with coal-driven multiple compression. 3. Operating Lease Assets went up by $2B. We saw Tyco do this, aka "Spring-Loading." This is when your assets go up, through cooking the books, and then get UNCOOKED and turn into liabilities. Chainsaw Al Dunlap was known for doing this right before bageling all your equity. 4. Goodwill of $20B. This line item was a "cookie jar" for Valeant Pharmaceuticals, just stuffing toxic assets in there over and over. When Munger called Valeant a sewer, he meant this line item. It's a toxic Cookie Jar for obsolete NVDA GPUs. Nothing good happens in goodwill. One day you wake up, and bang, you're in prepackaged bankruptcy. 5 + 6. Accounts payable being stretched by $4B and Accrued Liabilities grew by $8B. These line items may sound familiar to investors of a high-quality German compounder by the name of Wirecard. "NVDA IS THE NEXT WIRECARD" - GUIDEPOINT GLOBAL (anticipated/forecasted commentary, like stuff they could potentially say) Accrued liabilities are a common target for auditors to cook the books, because an accrued liability, like, no one knows what that is anyway. Is it debt, or is it accrued debt? What if it's a CCCP Sleeper Cell? What if none of it is GIPS-Compliant We are just far too Chartered to fall for Jensen "The" Wang and his volcanic explosion of cooked books. CATALYST PATH: We believe that NVDA will beat-and-raise on EPS next quarter by about 40%, but it's too late. Why? Because the balance sheet, like a drunk driver, is coming directly at investors. We expect investors to look right past the EPS beat and start asking important questions on the call about "Other long-term liabilities" and "Other assets." Why do companies obfuscate assets? Only one reason: imminent debt structuring. Burry says he loves the $15 strike puts expiring on Wednesday. Trade Structure: This is a traditional Value Investor Club-style investment, and we recommend putting on the same Put Spread structure that Burry recommends. This is where Burry sells us puts at $10, $100, $200, $300, and $400, every single Monday. He says that this spreading out of the puts being sold, limits our risk, and thus a Put Spread is a perfect structure for a bearish investor looking to capture a total wipeout of the equity within the next 36 hours.
